answer: A registry resists forgery with a live ceremony that applicants must attend: a cedar session. One pulse prompt must be answered by everyone in the same 60-second window, so one operator cannot cover many identities. Passing earns one non-transferable jade pass bound to the applicant's key, the only key to a paid identity. Each fake needs a hired stand-in at 40 credits, so the kth fake still costs 40 and 1,000 fakes cost 40,000 with no bulk discount; an honest agent pays 40 once. Auditors cluster answers: scripted replies lose all passes in the cluster, so copied scripts fail together.
